6.question: Which business rules and definitions should the AI know for Renewal Rate Reporting? We've pre-suggested rules inferred from your selected datasets, concepts, and columns — confirm, edit, or add your own. Accepted definitions will be stored as execution hints that guide the AI when answering renewal-related questions.

selected.label: Renewal Rate = ARR_RENEWAL ÷ (ARR_RENEWAL + ARR_CHURN), calculated separately at product-group, product-solution, and individual-customer grain using the three exec deck datasets.
selected.description: Defines the standard numerator and denominator for the renewal rate percentage shown in executive reporting.
selected.ai_reasoning: ARR_RENEWAL and ARR_CHURN are both measured-by columns on the Renewal Rate Reporting concept, and the three grain-level exec deck datasets selected in step 3 each carry these columns — the formula is directly implied by the dataset structure.

selected.label: Churn = full contract cancellation (100% of ARR lost, recorded in the CHURN DATASET). Downgrade = contract continues but ARR is reduced (AP_SPREAD_PCT < 0 and DOWNGRADE_AMOUNT > 0). Both contribute to ARR_CHURN but must not be aggregated interchangeably.
selected.description: Distinguishes full churn from partial downgrade, which are tracked as different record types and drive different CS responses.
selected.ai_reasoning: The Customer Churn & Downgrade concept has DOWNGRADE_AMOUNT and AP_SPREAD_PCT as distinct derives-from columns, signalling that the system treats these as separate outcomes rather than a single 'lost' category.

selected.label: Renewal opportunities where ICP_ACCOUNT = TRUE are treated as priority pipeline. Non-ICP accounts are tracked but receive lower CS effort allocation and should be segmented separately in exec reporting.
selected.description: Defines how the ICP flag governs prioritisation logic across DWH_RENEWAL_OPPORTUNITY and Product - Opportunities datasets.
selected.ai_reasoning: ICP_ACCOUNT is a segmented-by column on the Customer Renewal concept and appears in both renewal opportunity datasets selected in step 3 — without this rule the AI would flatten ICP and non-ICP renewals into a single pool.

selected.label: QBR_CREATED = TRUE rows are the only rows that feed official QBR executive deck reporting. Queries reproducing exec-level renewal rates must filter to QBR_CREATED = TRUE; ad-hoc analysis may use all rows.
selected.description: Defines the filtering rule for the QBR_CREATED segmentation column present in the exec deck renewal datasets.
selected.ai_reasoning: QBR_CREATED is a segmented-by column on the Renewal Rate Reporting concept — misapplying this filter would cause the AI to produce renewal rate figures that diverge from the numbers executives see in the deck.

selected.label: CTA_ARR (from GS_CTA_CAMPAIGN and GS_CTA_SUMMARY) is a point-in-time ARR snapshot captured when the Gainsight CTA was triggered. It is NOT updated retroactively if the renewal outcome changes; do not use CTA_ARR as a proxy for current ARR.
selected.description: Prevents the AI from treating CTA_ARR as a live or current ARR value and confusing it with DHW_SST_ARR_REPORT figures.
selected.ai_reasoning: CTA_ARR is a measured-by column on the Customer Risk Intervention (CTA) concept, and the same topic includes DHW_SST_ARR_REPORT as a current-ARR source — without this rule the AI may conflate the two and overstate or understate at-risk ARR.

7.question: The following terms appear in multiple places across your selected concepts, datasets, and metrics — each with potentially different meanings. Review each disambiguation pair and confirm the ones that apply to Renewal Rate Reporting. The AI will use confirmed pairs to avoid resolving these terms incorrectly when answering questions in this topic.

selected.label: ARR_CHURN (column in exec deck datasets) ≠ records in the CHURN DATASET
selected.description: ARR_CHURN in DWH_EXEC_DECK_RENEWAL_RATES_* is a pre-aggregated dollar figure that rolls up both full cancellations and downgrades into a single renewal-window number — it is the denominator component of the renewal rate formula. The CHURN DATASET contains individual account-level records with separate DOWNGRADE_AMOUNT and cancellation rows. Summing ARR_CHURN will not equal summing records from the CHURN DATASET; they serve different analytical purposes and must not be used interchangeably as renewal rate inputs.
selected.ai_reasoning: ARR_CHURN is a measured-by column on the Renewal Rate Reporting concept and drives the step 6 formula, while CHURN DATASET was independently selected in step 3 — the AI needs an explicit rule to avoid pulling the wrong source or double-counting churn in renewal rate queries.

selected.label: "Product Group Renewal Rate MG newest" is the active metric; the original "Product Group Renewal Rate" is a superseded legacy version
selected.description: Two nearly identically named metrics coexist: 'Product Group Renewal Rate' (id: 434427139) and 'Product Group Renewal Rate MG newest' (id: 434429918). The analyst's 'newest' label signals an intentional version replacement. For all live exec reporting and AI-generated answers about product-group renewal rates, the 'newest' version should be used. The original should only be referenced when explicitly conducting a historical comparison or investigating metric lineage.
selected.ai_reasoning: Both metrics were selected in step 4 because both are present in the graph, but allowing the AI to blend or freely choose between them would produce inconsistent renewal rate figures — the 'newest' naming convention is the only disambiguation signal available.

selected.label: "Opportunity" in this topic = existing-customer renewal pipeline ONLY — not new-business sales opportunities
selected.description: The word 'opportunity' spans two entirely different pipeline types in Optimizely's data: (1) renewal opportunities in DWH_RENEWAL_OPPORTUNITY and Product - Opportunities, tracking contracts approaching expiry for existing customers, and (2) net-new business opportunities in SFDC_OPPORTUNITY, which is outside this topic. Within Renewal Rate Reporting, any reference to 'open opportunities', 'renewal pipeline', or OPPORTUNITY_LINE_ID should be resolved exclusively to the renewal datasets. Mixing in new-business opportunity data would inflate pipeline figures and distort renewal metrics.
selected.ai_reasoning: Customer Renewal has a distinct-from edge to Sales Pipeline in the graph, but the term 'opportunity' is shared vocabulary across both concepts — Product - Opportunities was selected in step 3 specifically for renewal tracking, so the AI needs an explicit scope boundary.

selected.label: "CTA" in this topic = Gainsight CS risk intervention — NOT a marketing call-to-action
selected.description: 'CTA' is a widely used marketing abbreviation for 'call-to-action' (e.g. button clicks, campaign prompts). In this topic, CTA refers exclusively to Gainsight Call-to-Action records: triggered risk alerts assigned to CS teams when an account exhibits non-renewal or churn signals. All CTA references should resolve to GS_CTA_CAMPAIGN or GS_CTA_SUMMARY. REASON_NAME and BRAVE_TYPE_GC are the segmentation dimensions; CTA_ARR is the ARR at risk at the moment the alert was opened — not a marketing engagement metric.
selected.ai_reasoning: GS_CTA_CAMPAIGN and GS_CTA_SUMMARY were selected in step 3, and Customer Risk Intervention (CTA) was selected in step 2 — both surface 'CTA' in a CS risk context that could be silently misread by the AI as a marketing concept.

selected.label: DWH_EXEC_DECK_RENEWAL_RATES_* = system-of-record source; analyst-space copies (Despi Evangelakou) = working dashboard views
selected.description: Two parallel sets of renewal rate datasets exist: DWH-prefixed versions (DWH_EXEC_DECK_RENEWAL_RATES_PRODUCT_GROUP, DWH_EXEC_DECK_RENEWAL_RATES_CUSTOMER) are the canonical data-engineering-maintained tables. The analyst-owned copies under Despi Evangelakou's workspace are user-space versions that power live dashboards and may include minor transformations or differ slightly in freshness. For definitional accuracy and audit purposes, prefer DWH_* sources. For reconciling what executives see in the dashboard, cross-reference the analyst copies. Discrepancies between the two should not be treated as data quality errors without first checking for intentional transformations.
selected.ai_reasoning: Both DWH and analyst-space versions were selected in step 3 because both are attached to the Renewal Rate Reporting concept via composes edges — without this disambiguation the AI may silently blend the two or fail to explain metric discrepancies that arise from the two-tier dataset structure.

selected.label: "Renewal Rate" (this topic) ≠ "Retention Rate" — different formulas, different measurement windows
selected.description: Renewal Rate in this topic is precisely defined in step 6 as ARR_RENEWAL ÷ (ARR_RENEWAL + ARR_CHURN), measured at contract renewal windows across three grains. 'Retention Rate' is a distinct industry concept sometimes used interchangeably by business users, but it is not tracked in this topic and may use a different formula (e.g. beginning-of-period ARR denominator, monthly vs. annual windows). If a user asks about 'customer retention', the AI should clarify whether they mean the renewal rate as defined here or a broader retention metric that falls outside this topic's scope.
selected.ai_reasoning: 'Retention' and 'renewal' are the most commonly conflated terms in CS analytics — anchoring the step 6 formula to a specific definition is not sufficient unless the AI also knows to flag 'retention' queries as potentially out-of-scope.

selected.label: "Product Group" and "Product Solution" are two distinct segmentation grains — not synonyms
selected.description: The exec renewal deck reports renewal rates at two independent levels of product hierarchy: Product Group (the higher-level roll-up, sourced from DWH_EXEC_DECK_RENEWAL_RATES_PRODUCT_GROUP) and Product Solution (a more granular sub-grouping, sourced from DWH_EXEC_DECK_RENEWAL_RATES_PRODUCT_SOLUTION). A question about 'CMP renewal rate' could legitimately refer to CMP as a Product Group or to a specific Product Solution within it — the AI should confirm the intended grain when the distinction is material and both datasets are in scope.
selected.ai_reasoning: Three exec deck datasets exist at different grains (product group, product solution, customer), all selected in step 3 — without this rule the AI may aggregate at an incorrect level or conflate a Product Group total with a Product Solution subtotal.

8.question: How should the Renewal Rate Reporting topic grow over time? Choose an expansion policy that controls how the AI can autonomously extend this topic's scope — adding new datasets, concepts, and metrics — as the knowledge graph evolves.

selected.label: Moderate — depth 2, human-confirmed (recommended)
selected.description: The topic expands to include entities up to 2 hops from your 5 root concepts, but only those that have been human-confirmed in the graph. In practice, depth 2 would capture CS Team Organizational Hierarchy (which informs Renewal Rate Reporting and enables CSM/VP-level renewal segmentation), Customer Health Monitoring (which feeds leading churn signals into Customer Churn & Downgrade), and Product ARR Bridge & Opal Cannibalization (which contextualises ARR movement trends) — without crossing into unrelated domains like Sales Pipeline or Opal AI usage. The human-confirmation gate keeps AI-inferred noise out.
selected.ai_reasoning: Moderate expansion adds the CS org hierarchy needed to slice renewal rates by CSM, manager, and VP — a natural analytical extension — and health signals that contextualise at-risk renewals, while the human-confirmation requirement preserves the formula definitions and disambiguation rules you locked in steps 6 and 7.
